questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

The manager insisted that the files be reviewed (1)/ before they are submitted (2)/ to the committee (3)/ tomorrow morning. (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence lies in the incorrect verb tense in part **2**.
 
• The clause "**before they are submitted**" uses the present tense "**are**," which is inconsistent with the subjunctive mood triggered by "**insisted**."
 
• In formal English, when a verb like "insisted" is used, the subjunctive mood requires the base form of the verb "**be**" instead of "are."
 
• The correct phrase should be "**before they be submitted**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The manager insisted that the files be reviewed before they be submitted to the committee tomorrow morning."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "The manager insisted that the files be reviewed"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not need any changes.
 
• **3: "to the committee"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not need any changes.
 
• **4: "tomorrow morning"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not need any changes.

questions.question:

__
 
• The verb "**begin**" is incorrect in the context of the sentence as it is in the present tense.
 
• Since the sentence uses "**Hardly had the meeting started**," which indicates past perfect tense, the verb in the following clause should be in the past tense as well.
 
• The correct verb is "**began**" to maintain tense consistency.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 3** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Hardly had the meeting started when several members **began** raising objections to the proposal."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part 1: "Hardly had the meeting started"** – This part is correct as it uses the past perfect tense appropriately.
 
• **Part 2: "when several members"** – This part is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Part 4: "to the proposal"** – This part is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

The policy is believed to have been revised by the authorities.

options.text: Authorities are believed to have revised the policy.
It is believed the policy revises itself.
The policy believes it was revised.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**. 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 
__ 

• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence. 

• In this case, the passive voice sentence was: "The policy is believed to have been revised by the authorities." 

• To convert to active voice, place the subject "authorities" at the beginning. 

• The verb "is believed" remains unchanged as it reflects perception. 

• Ensure the object "the policy" follows the verb "to have revised" as the action performed by the authorities. 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**. 
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"Authorities are believed to have revised the policy."* 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 
 

• **Option 2: **"The policy was revised earlier." – This is incorrect as it changes the context of the sentence. 

• **Option 3: **"It is believed the policy revises itself." – This is incorrect as it alters the meaning entirely. 

• **Option 4: **"The policy believes it was revised." – This is incorrect as it personifies the policy, which is not relevant here. 
</ul

questions.question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

She __is owning__ this house since 2010.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**has owned**'. 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 
__ 
 
• The correct usage of the verb in this sentence is the present perfect tense "**has owned**." 
 
• The sentence indicates an action that started in the past ("**since 2010**") and continues into the present, which requires the present perfect tense. 
 
• **Option 1: "owns"** is incorrect because the action is ongoing since the past, not a simple present action. 
 
• **Option 2: "owned"** is incorrect because it suggests the action happened in the past and is no longer true. 
 
• **Option 4: "is owning"** is incorrect because "own" is a stative verb and is not used in the continuous form. 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**. 
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"She **has owned**__ this house since 2010."* 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
 
 
• **Option 1: "owns"** is incorrect because it does not reflect the ongoing nature of the action since 2010. 
 
• **Option 2: "owned"** is incorrect because it implies the ownership ended at some point in the past. 
 
• **Option 4: "is owning"** is incorrect because "own" is a stative verb and cannot be used in the continuous form. 
</ul

questions.question:
Select the correct option for the Direct Speech conversion of the sentence below:

He stated that the plan would have succeeded if resources had been adequate.

options.text: He said, “The plan would have succeeded if resources had been adequate.”
He said, “The plan succeeds with adequate resources.”
He said, “If resources are adequate, the plan will succeed.”
He said, “The plan had succeeded earlier.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He stated that the plan would have succeeded if resources had been adequate.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"that the plan would have succeeded if resources had been adequate" becomes "The plan would have succeeded if resources had been adequate."**
 
 
• The reporting clause "He stated that" is converted to "He said" in direct speech.
 
• The tense "would have succeeded" remains unchanged as it is a hypothetical situation in the past.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: "stated"
 
• Converted to: "said" to maintain the conversational tone in direct speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "The" and ends with a period "." inside the quotation marks.
 
• Reporting clause follows the quoted speech, separated by a comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He said, ‘The plan would have succeeded if resources had been adequate.’"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "He said, ‘The plan succeeds with adequate resources.’" 
 
 
• Changes the tense and meaning by implying a general truth instead of a past hypothetical scenario.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "He said, ‘If resources are adequate, the plan will succeed.’" 
 
 
• Incorrect tense: Changes the original hypothetical past situation to a future conditional.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "He said, ‘The plan had succeeded earlier.’" 
 
 
• Incorrect meaning: Suggests a completed past event instead of a hypothetical past success.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
A sentence is provided in direct speech. Choose the correct indirect form:

She said, “Where have you kept the documents?”

options.text: She asked where I kept the documents.
She asked where I have kept the documents.
She asked where I had kept the documents.
She asked where had I kept the documents.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She asked where I had kept the documents.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"Where have you kept" becomes "where I had kept"**
 
 
• The present perfect tense "have kept" changes to the past perfect tense "had kept" in indirect speech.
 
• Pronoun "you" is changed to "I" to match the indirect speech perspective.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Direct: "She said"
 
• Converted to: "She asked" to indicate a question was asked.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is converted to indirect speech without quotation marks.
 
• The word order is adjusted to match indirect question format.
 
• The question mark is removed as it is no longer a direct question.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *She asked where I had kept the documents.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "She asked where I kept the documents."
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "kept" does not reflect the present perfect tense of the original direct sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "She asked where I have kept the documents."
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "have kept" does not follow the rule of changing present perfect to past perfect in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "She asked where had I kept the documents."
 
 
• Incorrect word order: In indirect speech, the subject "I" should come before the verb "had kept."
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Rearrange the following sentences to make a logical sequence:

1. Regular practice strengthens habits.

2. Change requires conscious effort.

3. Identifying weaknesses is essential.

4. Support systems aid consistency.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct sequence is **2-3-4-1** based on logical flow.
 
• Let us analyze the sentences:
 
 
• **Sentence 2**: "Change requires conscious effort." This is the starting sentence as it introduces the need for change, which is the foundation of the discussion.
 
• **Sentence 3**: "Identifying weaknesses is essential." This follows next, emphasizing the importance of analyzing one's shortcomings for effective change.
 
• **Sentence 4**: "Support systems aid consistency." This comes next, highlighting the role of external help in maintaining progress.
 
• **Sentence 1**: "Regular practice strengthens habits." This concludes the sequence by focusing on the final step: the reinforcement of habits through regular practice.
 
 
• The logical sequence ensures a smooth progression of thought from change initiation to habit formation.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"Change requires conscious effort. Identifying weaknesses is essential. Support systems aid consistency. Regular practice strengthens habits."</div
